node.statement: Because mu and sigma are continuous, mu(calU_e x calU_e) is connected and contains mu(J,J)=J, while sigma(calU_e) is connected and contains sigma(J)=J; hence both images lie in calU_e. Likewise the smooth scalar action preserves calU_e. This U(1)-action is free: a unitary U has a right inverse and so U is nonzero, whence cU=U implies c=1. It is proper: for the action graph map (c,U)|->(cU,U), the inverse image of a compact K is a closed subset of the compact set U(1) x pr_2(K). Thus lem-topology-quotient-manifold gives the quotient map p:calU_e->breve-calU as a smooth surjective submersion. Equivariance gives p(mu(cU,dV))=p(mu(U,V)) and p(sigma(cU))=p(sigma(U)), so the displayed breve-mu and breve-sigma are well-defined. They are smooth: local smooth sections of the submersions p x p and p express them locally as p o mu o (s_1,s_2) and p o sigma o s, and equivariance makes these local expressions agree. Finally (A_5) gives breve-mu(breve-e,[U])=[U]=breve-mu([U],breve-e) and breve-sigma(breve-e)=breve-e.
